SUSPICIOUS DEATH
BDM Montreal — Mile End Branch
Entrepôt des Érablières, Montreal
Suspicious death
Night watchman
Forklift operator.
I drive the forklift; I don’t count barrels.

At nine I plugged it in to charge and left. The foreman keeps the second forklift’s key; he doesn’t give it to anyone. Last month he said, ‘I’ll stack the barrels, don’t you touch them,’ row fourteen. I asked why; ‘grading,’ he said. I didn’t crush anyone. My forklift was charging.
She fiddles with the zip of her vest.
Did you use your forklift this evening?
Kayla Fortin — interview
Foreman.
I’ve run this warehouse for thirty years.
No.
The record’s right there: twelve hundred barrels, complete. I counted, the president approved. If I had nothing to hide, why would I kill anyone?

Half of row fourteen is water. Six years, a bit every year. A man from Laurentide said, ‘Make sure the stock is complete on paper, we’ll handle the rest’; the premium was paid, the syrup sold. Hélène found the row. I took the second forklift, raised the forks to the top rack and pushed. I put the key in my pickup. Next morning I was going to write ‘complete’ on the count again.
You toppled the barrels onto Hélène.

I was in the office, paperwork. I told the inspector, ‘The racks are high, it’s dangerous at night’; she didn’t listen. Tapping and tapping at the barrels with her mallet, she shifted the stack and it toppled.
He tugs at his moustache with his lower lip.

The victim’s husband.
Hélène didn’t bring her work home.

She didn’t tell me things, but last night at dinner she said, ‘The foreman didn’t want to let me into the warehouse at night; I insisted.’ ‘If they’ve emptied half the barrels and filled them with water, the insurance is a lie too,’ she said. I laughed. I shouldn’t have laughed.
He takes off his glasses and holds them in his palm.

On the night of 9 November 2030, at the Entrepôt des Érablières warehouse north of Montreal, the syrup grading inspector Hélène Côté (58) was found dead under a stack of barrels that had toppled from a high rack. Water poured from two burst barrels.

The night watchman Minh Tran found the body at 23.40 when he heard the noise. In the warehouse that evening: foreman Réjean Gauthier, forklift operator Kayla Fortin. The cooperative’s president Claudette Marceau and the victim’s husband Paul Leblanc arrived during the night.
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the autopsy report
Request the warehouse stock count record
Request permission to search the foreman’s pickup and office

The record was a decoy: the signature didn’t clear the foreman, it showed who owned the lie. The watchman, the operator and the camera pointed to the forklift; the president and the husband to the motive. The search found the key in the sun visor.
The record was complete. The barrels weren’t.
Entrepôt des Érablières — November 2030

For six years the foreman Réjean Gauthier sold the syrup from the barrels in row fourteen and filled them with coloured water; he wrote the count record as ‘complete’ himself, and the insurance premiums were paid as if on real stock. The inspector Hélène Côté, called in by the cooperative, found the row by tapping the barrels with a mallet. Gauthier took the second forklift, pushed the barrels on the top rack onto her and hid the key in his pickup.
Who killed Hélène Côté?
FILE #062  /  BUBE MONTREAL — MILE END
File #062 — Syrup Warehouse
Night watchman.
At night I’m at the gate.

Around 23.30, the sound of a forklift, then a huge crash. I ran; Kayla’s forklift was in its place, charging. The second forklift was at the end of the aisle, with no ignition key. There’s a camera in the warehouse facing the back aisle; I don’t watch the screen, it records.
He straightens his glasses with both hands.
What did you hear during the night?
Minh Tran — interview

Réjean Gauthier’s pickup and his office at the warehouse (with the branch chief’s approval):

· Behind the pickup’s sun visor, the second forklift’s ignition key; Réjean Gauthier’s fingerprint and syrup on the key.
· In the office cupboard, drums of colouring liquid and empty syrup barrel lids.
· On his phone, to a number at Laurentide Réassurance, 9 November 23.52: ‘The inspector won’t be a problem.’
